- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.1), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > 0.1) after a downtrend, model underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days of forecast > true, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period (first 7–10 days); apply 1–2% downward correction to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.27” spikes, model tends to overreact; apply 1–3% dampening to forecast if sentiment is high and price is rising.
